SLOOS-informed assessment:
- Policy stance: Hawkish. The FOMC raised the target range 75 bp to 3–3.25%, lifted administered rates (IORB/ON RRP), and reaffirmed balance-sheet runoff, signaling ongoing tightening amid elevated and broad-based inflation.
- Bank credit supply and demand (July 2022 SLOOS):
  - C&I: Banks tightened standards and terms for firms of all sizes and increased loan costs and collateralization; many cited a weaker economic outlook, liquidity concerns, and industry-specific issues. Despite this, banks reported stronger C&I loan demand (including at foreign banks).
  - CRE: Banks tightened standards across CRE categories, with banks reporting weaker CRE loan demand.
  - Household credit: Banks tightened standards for GSE-eligible and jumbo mortgages, HELOCs, credit cards, and subprime auto; demand strengthened for HELOCs but broader mortgage-related demand softened.
- Implications: The SLOOS shows monetary tightening is transmitting into tighter bank credit, raising the effective restrictiveness of financial conditions. This amplifies downside risks to growth relative to the FOMC’s “modest growth” characterization, even as inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Net effect: Compared with a macro-only read, SLOOS tilts the outlook further negative due to tighter credit availability and higher borrowing costs. Adjusting for SLOOS, overall tone is more negative.
